newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan's economic recovery becoming firmer -- EPA.
newsitem.headline: Japan's economic recovery becoming firmer -- EPA.

text.p: Japan's economic recovery is becoming slightly firmer compared to the summer months, Economic Planning Agency Vice Minister Shimpei Nukaya told a news conference on Friday.
"Compared to the economic movement during the summer, the recovery is becoming slightly firmer," he said.
Nukaya said although consumption was a bit weak earlier in the summer, it had rebounded in August and September.
Industrial production, as seen in recent figures, was growing and inventory adjustments were coming to an end, he said.

Nukaya said it would be "reassuring" if this meant that the economic cycle was moving towards one led by private-sector demand, rather than by policy measures, especially at a time when public-works spending was expected to decline.
He added that he would also be reassured even if such an economic recovery was only gradual.
Commenting on September's unemployment data, Nukaya said the unemployment situation could not be expected to improve overnight, but added that the rate appeared to have peaked and to be heading down.
Asked whether the weaker yen against the dollar would create inflationary pressure in Japan, he said:
"The situation now is not such that we need to worry about a weak yen affecting prices."
Prices of imported goods had risen but they had not affected overall prices in Japan, he said.
Nukaya said the pace of the decline in the current account surplus in coming months would not be as sharp as it used to be, but added:
"We are not at a stage where the surplus is expected to expand."
